basis: The 2020 report gives 14 social security agreements with EU Member States and the 2021 report gives 13 out of the same total of 23, while the 2021 report also states there were no changes in this area (MKD-EU-2021-001-0068).

The 2023 report gives 23 bilateral agreements in place, while the ministry list, whose file is dated February 2023, shows 22 concluded agreements plus six conventions taken over from the former SFRY, which does not give 23 on either count (the list states no total).

The 2023 report gives 23 bilateral agreements, while North Macedonia states 22 in the screening report, whose bilateral meeting took place in March 2023, and no item under this issue records an agreement ending.

The Commission states that the law does not distinguish between EU citizens and other foreigners, while North Macedonia states that under the same law the quotas do not apply to EU citizens following a reciprocity agreement with the EU.

The 2024 report states that only nine named Member States have citizens with access to medical services, while the 2025 report names fourteen as having obtained that access and also states there was no development (MKD-EU-2025-001-0108).

The 2021 report gives 593 of 3 672 work permits for EU citizens in 2020, which is about 16%, while North Macedonia states an EU citizen share of 12,8% for 2020; neither item defines its denominator further.
The negotiations with Italy and Greece, reported in 2024, match the Commission recommendation from 2021 onwards to conclude further agreements with Member States.
The screening report states that the Employment Service Agency will act as EURES National Coordination Office, which is part of the organisational arrangements for joining EURES.
The screening report states that the amendments are intended to comply fully with EURES standards.
The planned analysis of harmonisation needs is stated directly after the finding that national legislation has no system for appointing EURES members and partners.
The 2023 report describes the capacity building as being for civil servants who will work on EURES.
The screening report states that the twinning project trained Employment Service Agency staff on EURES in 2014 and 2015.
The screening report lists the strengthening of Employment Agency capacities among the plans in its EURES section.
The screening report states that the IT and database upgrade is so that the Agency can be the only point for exchanging data with EURES.
The 2023 report describes the capacity building as being for civil servants who will work on the European Labour Authority.
The screening report states the plan to harmonise with the European Labour Authority regulation directly after finding national legislation not aligned with it.
The screening report states that the preparations are so that the State Labour Inspectorate can respond to tasks coordinated by the European Labour Authority.
The screening report states a plan to amend the legislation to harmonise it with the EU acquis, as part of its social security coordination plans.
The screening report states a plan to analyse capacity and IT infrastructure and to define the access points with EESSI.
North Macedonia reports the planned registry in its presentation on electronic exchange of social security information, in the screening report section on that subject.
The 2020 report states that the single application process was further simplified by the amendments in force from May 2019.
The Commission states that the experience gathered through the bilateral agreements allows a good level of preparation on social security coordination.
The Commission states that various bilateral agreements allow EU citizens to use the European Health Insurance Card in North Macedonia.
The source states that because healthcare facilities have no EHIC reader the data cannot be processed electronically.
The Commission report and the Employment Service Agency report both give 755 work permits issued in 2021.
The table of concluded agreements in the ministry list has 22 rows, 13 of them with EU Member States, and the Commission report gives 22 agreements of which 13 are with EU Member States.
The Commission report and North Macedonia in the screening report name the same nine Member States for use of the European Health Insurance Card or the related access to medical services.
The Commission report and North Macedonia in the screening report both state that public posts are closed apart from exceptions in health and, with -0023 of the screening report, higher education.
The Commission report and North Macedonia in the screening report both state that the Employment Agency has not adopted or signed the integrity policy.
The Commission report and North Macedonia in the screening report both state that family reunification is allowed for foreign workers.
The international report and the Commission report both state that North Macedonia uses a quota for work permits.
